$comment: The ADR-0002 bypass suite, declared. Every row in the ADR's B1-B18 table appears here exactly
once, and `status` says whether it is asserted today or owed to a later milestone.
`live`    — a test in `provenBy` executes this row's assertion against a real database.
`pending` — not yet assertable; `pendingUntil` names the milestone that unblocks it and
`reason` says what is missing. A row is never deferred silently (plan line 71).
Wording note: implementation-plan M1-AC8 words the two states `implemented` and
`pending: <milestone>`. Same two states, split into two fields so the milestone is data
rather than a substring to parse.
This file is the source of truth for `pnpm test:security`, which reports all eighteen row
IDs with their state. Deleting a row fails the run — see b-row-manifest.security.test.ts.

rows.title: anon/authenticated cannot read schema app
rows.assertion: Connecting as `anon` and as `authenticated` and selecting from every table in `app` raises SQLSTATE 42501. Fails if the enumerated table count is 0.

rows.title: PostgREST cannot reach schema app
rows.assertion: A request to the Supabase REST endpoint for every table in `app` with a valid user JWT returns 404 / PGRST106, for `anon`, `authenticated` and `service_role`, on reads, writes and RPC, and the OpenAPI document advertises no `app` relation. Catalog-driven, and PostgREST is started from `supabase/config.toml`'s own `[api] schemas`, so exposing `app` fails.

rows.title: Full policy-shape and privilege assertion
rows.assertion: For every table in `app`: relrowsecurity, relforcerowsecurity, relowner = app_migrator, and exactly one pg_policies row `app_rw_full_access` / PERMISSIVE / {app_rw} / ALL / qual true / with_check true. Plus app_rw is not super, cannot bypass RLS, and holds no pg_auth_members row; plus the ADR-0002 §3 revoke set is in force.

rows.title: No unallowlisted SECURITY DEFINER function in app
rows.assertion: No SECURITY DEFINER function exists in `app` unless listed in `security-definer-allowlist.json`, keyed by full `regprocedure` signature so an allowlisted name does not pre-authorize its future overloads; a stale entry naming no live function fails too. The `SET search_path` requirement is asserted over every function in `app` by the ADR-0002 section 5 test in the same file, which is a superset.

rows.title: Visibility matrix, including the §6a person-projection sub-case
rows.assertion: For the graph read, a viewer with no relationship to either party of a connection gets 0 rows, and a person below `full` disclosure renders with no name, handle, or avatar (ADR-0002 §6a). Scoped to the graph surface, which is what L2 built: the board, search, and notification surfaces of the same rule need `modules/bulletins` and are owed by L3a, which extends this row and this assertion text when it lands.

rows.title: Directional trust never leaves the holder
rows.assertion: A trust value and its field name appear nowhere in any payload returned to the other party or a third party, at any nesting depth, across success, error, and conflict envelopes.

rows.title: Blocking is total, including the flush and offline boundaries
rows.assertion: After A blocks B neither sees the other, no graph path routes through the blocked edge, no notification is deliverable, and a push computed before the block is not flushed after it.
rows.reason: Corrected from M2, not deferred from it: this row's own text already said it completes at M5. The M2 half is asserted today - blocking has no entity in M2, so there is nothing here an M2 test could execute. The flush boundary needs ADR-0006's scheduled queue to be observable and the offline boundary needs ADR-0005 sync replay against a blocked subject; both are M5 (M5-AC2).

rows.title: Hidden people leak nothing but topology
rows.assertion: A ghost payload contains no name, handle, avatar, role, mutual count, or real internal ID; surrogates differ across viewers; a re-identification fixture holds against ADR-0004's adjacency rule.
rows.reason: Corrected from M2, not deferred from it: this row's own text already said it completes at M5. The payload half is asserted today by the visibility matrix's ADR-0002 section 6a sub-case (tests/security/visibility-matrix.security.test.ts) - a person below full disclosure renders with no name, handle, or avatar. The structural re-identification fixture needs the full graph model and surrogate identifiers, which land at M5 (M5-AC3).

rows.title: Report privacy
rows.assertion: The reported author's every read path — bulletin, notifications, audit, API, operator-mediated surfaces — contains no reporter identity.

rows.title: A filter can narrow but never widen
rows.assertion: A Notify Me query or board query crafted to reference a non-authorized author, tag, or bulletin returns 0 rows rather than an error-free leak.

rows.title: Erased users leave no reachable personal data
rows.assertion: After erasure no query path returns their personal data, and stale offline mutations referencing them fail closed.
rows.reason: Erasure is an M5 capability (M5-AC4); nothing implements ADR-0008's erasure path yet.

rows.title: Composition assertion, plus the SQL-location secondary rule
rows.assertion: Every query implementation taking a `ViewerId` references `app.visible_people` / `app.visible_bulletins` or the shared authorized-set builder; secondary: no SQL outside `persistence/` and `supabase/`.

rows.title: Write-path IDOR matrix
rows.assertion: For every mutation type in ADR-0005's conflict matrix, an unrelated actor gets a structured failure with zero state change and zero outbox rows. Proven here for bulletin.archive, bulletin.undismiss, and notifyMe.update (bulletin.create is fail-closed by construction, asserted alongside them); connection.accept, trust.set, bulletin.report, and bulletin.dismiss remain owed to their owning lanes, completing at L5's confirmation pass (m2-lane-briefs.md:789), the same partial-coverage discipline B5's row already records. bulletin.undismiss (#170) is the second shape of genuine case: it is a DELETE, so an actor who legitimately passes every authorization check must still be unable to clear another viewer's dismissal, which only the viewer_id predicate in the statement enforces.

rows.title: viewerId provenance fitness
rows.assertion: No tRPC input schema on any procedure carries a viewerId/userId/actorId/ownerId field, asserted by walking the router type tree; and `ViewerId` has exactly one constructor, taking an `Actor`.

rows.title: Operator scope
rows.assertion: The operator path cannot read trust values or reporter identity reachable by a reported user, cannot write outside the four enumerated actions, and emits an audit entry per read.
rows.reason: The operator entrypoint and `app_operator_ro` role are M5 (M5-AC27). ADR-0002 §8 deliberately defers building them.

rows.title: Storage objects
rows.assertion: Direct bucket access as anon/authenticated is denied; a signed URL is minted only for an object the viewer may see under the §6a disclosure rule; TTL <= 5 minutes.
rows.reason: Nothing uploads a file before M5 — the M2 slice explicitly does not build storage (plan line 274, M5-AC33).

rows.title: Unauthorized is indistinguishable from non-existent
rows.assertion: Unauthorized and non-existent produce identical status, error code, and byte-identical bodies across single-entity fetch, `from:` resolution, intro-connector resolution, and report/dismiss of an invisible bulletin. Single-entity fetch is proven on both surfaces that have one: bulletins.getById (M2-AC14) and notes.getById (#176, decision D14). The note case carries a third input the bulletin case has no analogue for — the note's own author, who is refused byte-identically to a stranger because app.visible_notes gates on recipient_id = viewer_id, so a read that answered the author differently would turn the private channel's only fetch into the delivery receipt PDF §6 denies it. `from:` resolution and intro-connector resolution remain owed to M5, the same partial-coverage discipline B5's and B13's rows record.

rows.title: Post-deploy catalog smoke against the LIVE database
rows.assertion: B1, B3 and B4's assertions plus `current_user = session_user = 'app_rw'`, run against the deployed environment through the production connection path. Gates the M4.5 rollout.
rows.reason: There is no deployed environment. This row is the one that catches an API deployed as `postgres` (risk R13) and cannot be simulated against Testcontainers — that is precisely why the ADR separates it from B1/B3/B4.
